service: Hyper3D Rodin (hyper3d.ai), Business plan, through the hyper3d MCP server
prompt: A little toy robot built from a dented tin can: a fat cylindrical can body in matte silver-gray clay (not shiny metal) with one big round dent and a few dark rust-brown patches, two big round bolt eyes, a small funnel hat on top, two short chunky bent arms and two stubby wheel feet. Cute and homemade. Hand-sculpted matte modeling clay, stop-motion claymation style, chunky rounded forms. One single closed object, no base, no text, no logos.

files.model.fbx: Rodin's base_basic_pbr.fbx; its embedded diffuse map is the final one, and its normal, roughness and metallic maps are flat 1-pixel images (flat normal, roughness 0.85, not metallic), so the clay stays matte

credits: Rodin reports no cost per call; about 0.5 credit a generation (T81's measurement). T105's total is in Docs/tasks/T105.md.
note: Texture de-light on: the can came out near white rather than silver-gray. My person approved it as it is.
